observed_original_abi.calling_convention: UNNAMED BY DESIGN: 0 ordinary stack arguments, no register receiver, bare RET. The derived ABI record abstains (`no_discriminator: no stack-argument read and no positive receiver evidence`) and reports cdecl/stdcall/thiscall/fastcall as byte-identical, which is correct for a zero-parameter entry. This package therefore models it as a plain zero-parameter entry and does not pick one.
observed_original_abi.receiver: none. ECX is unreadable by construction: 0x00b3d380 is `a1 <disp32>` (MOV EAX, moffs32), which has no ModRM byte and therefore no r/m and no register operand at all.
observed_original_abi.return_type: opaque 32-bit object pointer; the pointee class is UNKNOWN
observed_original_abi.body_span: 0x00b3d380..0x00b3d386, 6 bytes (0xcc at 0x00b3d386 is INT3 pad, not part of the body)

observed_mechanics: 0x00b3d380: MOV EAX,dword ptr ds:[0x0167eb04] - a 32-bit LOAD of an absolute .data word, not a LEA and not an immediate
no branch, no call, no flag test, no register save, no loop and no store anywhere in the 6-byte body
the read happens on every entry: no lazy path, no cache, no publication check, no default and no refresh
the slot is not written by this function, and neither is the pointee it returns

semantic_findings: The entry is a borrowed global-slot reader: one 32-bit load, one return, no validation, no reference counting, no write.

It has 240 direct callsites across 165 distinct caller functions in the committed xrefs export, the high-fan-in profile of the accessor block. Fan-in says nothing about the pointee's class and is not used as evidence for one.
The returned value is dereferenced as a pointer at offset 0x48 (bit 0 tested) by three independent callers, so the word is a pointer to an object with a flags byte there.
The slot is table offset 0x44 of the 0x0167eac0..0x0167eb68 singleton table whose 43 words each have one dedicated accessor; 0x00b3d220 independently returns the table base as an immediate.

No committed research note names this slot's pointee. Unlike its siblings DAT_0167eae0/DAT_0167eae4/DAT_0167eb0c/DAT_0167eb60, this slot is absent from docs/analysis/simulator-root-closure.md, knowledgegraph/research/root-closure/followup-global-slots.md and knowledgegraph/research/root-closure/followup-receiver-provenance.md.

unresolved_questions: What class does the word at 0x0167eb04 point to? No SDK import, committed research note or sampled caller names it.
Who publishes 0x0167eb04, and when relative to the 240 callsites that read it? No direct writer exists; indirect or bulk publication is unexcluded.
Is the byte at pointee+0x48 a flags word with more defined bits than bit 0? Three callers test only bit 0.
Are the 0x0167eb00 and 0x0167eb08 slots (accessors 0x00b3d370 and 0x00b3d390, immediate neighbours in the same table) related to this one? Neither is named.
Does the pointer the entry returns need an AddRef, and if so by whom? The body has no room for a reference call, and no writer is known, so ownership is undetermined.

focused_test.assertion_style: abort on the first failure; each group names the hypothesis it refutes
coverage: the return is the slot's stored VALUE, not the slot's address, not a constant, not zero
the returned word is usable as a pointer: result+0x48 reads the planted fixture byte, so a LEA-form or constant answer cannot also pass
the address is this slot: distinct sentinels on the neighbouring words, neither returned, neither disturbed
the body reads: the whole 5-word window AND the pointee are byte-identical before and after
a pure function of the slot: repeats, tracks changes, returns a published null unchanged, returns 0xffffffff and 0x11 verbatim
no register receiver and no stack argument, read off the encoding: 0xa1 is MOV EAX,moffs32, so there is no ModRM byte and no register operand, and the single memory operand is the absolute disp32
the callee pops nothing: the trailing byte is 0xc3 (RET, no imm16) and not 0xc2
the encoding is the observed six bytes and its disp32 is the header's kSlotVa
the single observed pointee offset 0x48 is inside the modelled fixture
focused_test.abi_claim_basis: encoding, not run-time sampling. An earlier draft sampled ESP around the call and re-called from a deeper frame via constrained inline asm; every version of that measurement was silently unreliable across -O levels and compilers (a callee-saved register allocated to an output and then overwritten by the harness's own `pop`, a variable alloca folded into one fixed frame so both depths were the same point, and a `call *%reg` whose target register the compiler allocated to the register being poisoned). For a body of `a1 <disp32>; c3` the encoding argument is strictly stronger and holds identically at every optimisation level, so the measurement was removed rather than kept flaky. This is recorded in the test file's header comment.
focused_test.build_matrix: clang++ and g++, -m32, -Wall -Wextra -Werror, -std=c++17, at -O0/-O1/-O2/-O3 and at the default level: all pass
